body.statement: There is a deterministic algorithm that, after \(2^{O(b\log b)}\operatorname{poly}(|V|+|E^{\mathrm{det}}|+|E^{?}|)\) preprocessing, enumerates every member of \(\mathcal O_{XY}\) exactly once with the same worst-case delay and polynomial working space; its first output and exhaustion obey the same bound, every output is globally minimal, and each output receives a canonical original-query ID failure label.
body.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel converting one uncertain causal graph into a complete, auditable antichain of failure explanations.
body.gap: The nearest causal algorithms return one optimal edge deletion or discover only the hedges needed for an intervention optimum; no cited result proves output-sensitive uncertain-edge support enumeration.
body.consumer: The uncertain-ADMG sampler and edgeID workflow can report every minimal jointly harmful edge combination rather than one selected identifiable realization.

obligation.what_is_open: The worst-case-delay, duplicate-free, polynomial-space enumerator in the general district-width parameter \(b\).
obligation.obstruction: Its declared dependency is the unresolved cross-core recursion. In addition, the OEQ's present phrase `finite state' does not itself guarantee the theorem's polynomial working-space bound; a positive resolution must bound the representation size explicitly.
obligation.attempted: Composing sparse-core generation with per-core minimal directed-support enumeration gives coverage but not bounded gaps after cross-core global-minimality filtering. Recomputing ID labels at outputs is polynomial and is not the obstruction.
obligation.partial_result: Coverage, global-minimum equivalence, the \(2^{O(b\log b)}\) core bound, and polynomial-time recomputation of an ordinary-ID failure label for any completed support are available.  The claimed worst-case delay and polynomial-space enumeration do not follow until the cross-core partial-support recursion has a polynomial-size state and a bounded-time nonempty-completion test.
